C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE.IntentSummary: Execute the approved C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE spec: pin a fence-before-open invariant in the single shared sandboxed writer — the last M-010 validation runs immediately before the only opening syscall, after all directory mutation, with no filesystem work in between — so parallel path mutation inside the workspace can no longer make a save land outside the sandbox. The writer re-fences after create_dir_all and denies, with the existing MT_FS_PATH_DENIED family, when the re-fence's canonical resolution differs from the first fence's validated path (this denies only links planted during the window; every pre-existing inward or outward resolution is unchanged between the fences and keeps its current allowance or denial). Deterministic race-shape regression tests inject leaf and ancestor mutation through a cfg(test)-only path-keyed hook, the save-and-close and document-snapshot routes prove the same refusal at their own layer, all allowed-symlink and denial regressions stay green unchanged, and the fs.rs contract, M-002/M-010 graph summaries and V-M-002/V-M-010 verification surfaces state the invariant, the residual single-pathwalk window and the per-platform follow-up direction honestly. m010_security stays stdlib-only with its fence unchanged; no new crate dependencies; write semantics (in-place write_all + sync_all, non-atomic, parent auto-creation) and all renderer-visible error codes are preserved.

Design decisions locked by this plan: (1) the re-fence is a second full check_path call on the same request string, placed after create_dir_all; the writer additionally denies when the re-fence's canonical result differs from the first fence's validated path — this implements deny-only-NEW-links: a link planted in the window changes the canonicalization (whether inward or outward) and is denied, while any resolution present before the window is identical at both fences and keeps its current behavior; check_path itself continues to deny now-outside resolutions directly; (2) the only opening syscall is fs::File::create on the re-fence's validated path; write_all + sync_all stay in place and non-atomic; (3) the deterministic seam is a cfg(test)-only race_window_hook, invoked exactly once between directory mutation and the re-fence, compiled to a no-op inline function outside test builds, settable via a cfg(test) pub(crate) set_race_window_hook keyed by the exact validated path so parallel tests on distinct TempDirs cannot cross-fire; (4) the differs-denial constructs SecurityError::SymlinkEscapesSandbox with the re-fence result as resolved and the first fence's result as sandbox, mapped through the existing from_security_path so the renderer-visible code stays MT_FS_PATH_DENIED, with a new BLOCK_REVALIDATION_CHANGED log marker in the BLOCK_ convention; (5) m010_security.rs takes no behavioral change — contract/LINKS notes and its test module only, stdlib-only preserved, no libc/rustix/windows-sys promotion; (6) fs_copy_inner, fs_move_inner, fs_mkdir_inner and the m047 bookmark rescue are outside the spec's writer scope and are not touched; (7) m005_prefs.rs is reference-only, no change planned; (8) the residual race is the single kernel pathwalk between the re-fence and File::create — stated in contract, graph and verification, not hidden. T-001.Title: Fence-before-open invariant in the shared writer (re-fence after directory mutation, deny resolution changes, open only the re-validated path)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Restructure write_validated_bytes in src-tauri/src/m013b/fs.rs to the exact order: (1) the unchanged first fence let validated = m010_security::check_path(sandbox, Path::new(path)) with from_security_path mapping; (2) the unchanged parent auto-creation fs::create_dir_all on validated.parent(); (3) the cfg(test)-only seam call race_window_hook(&validated); — a function that outside test builds is a #[cfg(not(test))] #[inline] no-op taking the validated path and inside test builds dispatches to a path-keyed action registered through a #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn set_race_window_hook (the hook fires only when the validated path exactly equals the registered key, so parallel tests on distinct TempDirs cannot cross-fire, and the setter returns the previous registration so tests restore the empty state); (4) the re-fence let revalidated = m010_security::check_path(sandbox, Path::new(path)) with the same from_security_path mapping — the last M-010 validation, running after all directory mutation; (5) the resolution-change denial if revalidated != validated — log safe_eprintln!("[FsCmd][write][BLOCK_REVALIDATION_CHANGED path={}]", redact(path)) and return Err(IpcError::from_security_path(cmd, SecurityError::SymlinkEscapesSandbox { resolved: revalidated.display().to_string(), sandbox: validated.display().to_string() })) so the renderer-visible code stays MT_FS_PATH_DENIED (from_security_path maps every SecurityError to MT_FS_PATH_DENIED, m013b/error.rs:80-87); (6) the only opening syscall fs::File::create(&revalidated) — opened on the path the last fence validated, with no filesystem work between the re-fence and the open (the comparison is pure); (7) the unchanged in-place file.write_all + file.sync_all. The three facades fs_write_inner, fs_write_bytes_inner, fs_write_binary_inner and the commands mt_fs_write, mt_fs_write_binary keep their signatures, logging and error contracts; write semantics stay non-atomic with parent auto-creation; no new crate dependency, no libc/rustix/windows-sys promotion, no IPC surface change; fs_copy_inner, fs_move_inner and fs_mkdir_inner are untouched.

Contract hygiene: the fs.rs START_MODULE_CONTRACT SCOPE records the fence-before-open invariant (last M-010 validation immediately before the only opening syscall, after all directory mutation, denying any canonical-resolution change introduced in the window) and states the residual single-pathwalk window between the re-fence and File::create honestly, plus the cfg(test) hook as declared test-only contract surface per spec Assumption 3; the LINKS line gains .grace/changes/active/C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE; CHANGE_SUMMARY gains a dated 2026-11-21 C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE entry; MODULE_MAP is updated if the lint requires the cfg(test) setter to be listed, with no lint regressions on the file. m010_security.rs takes NO behavioral change: its LINKS gains .grace/changes/active/C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE and its contract notes (SCOPE/STATUS area) record that writers re-fence immediately before open, that check_path and canonicalize_nearest_ancestor are byte-unchanged, that the module stays stdlib-only, and that std cannot hold a validated descriptor across the open (the honest per-platform statement from the spec's platform-honesty constraint); its CHANGE_SUMMARY gains the same dated entry. m001_save_close.rs CHANGE_SUMMARY gains the dated entry and the save/snapshot write-path comments state that both routes reach disk only through the hardened writer (the early ownership fence at line 337 stays exactly as it is). Every START_BLOCK_/END_BLOCK_ marker stays paired and unique across the codebase.

T-002.Title: Race-shape regressions (deterministic hook), route-level save refusals, red-first proof, allowance regressions green

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: fs.rs test module gains three #[cfg(unix)] race tests, each registering its action via set_race_window_hook keyed to its own TempDir-backed validated path and restoring the empty registration afterwards: race_leaf_outward_planted_denied (write to a missing nested leaf; the hook plants an outward symlink at the leaf, pointing at a preset outside target; assert the write returns MT_FS_PATH_DENIED, the outside target's content is byte-for-byte unchanged, and no regular file exists at the requested path — the planted link remains but nothing was written through it); race_ancestor_swapped_outward_denied (an existing inside directory component of the validated path is swapped by the hook to a symlink pointing at an outside directory; assert MT_FS_PATH_DENIED, the outside directory's content unchanged, and no file created at the joined outside path); race_leaf_inward_planted_denied (the hook plants an INWARD symlink at the leaf; assert MT_FS_PATH_DENIED — documenting the deny-only-NEW-links semantics: any canonical-resolution change in the window denies, while the pre-existing inward links of ancestor_inward_ok keep passing unchanged because both fences resolve them identically). Each test also asserts the failure leaves no partial file at the requested path.

m001_save_close.rs test module gains two #[cfg(unix)] route-level race tests using the same pub(crate) hook to prove the refusal propagates through the save routes, not only the writer: save_race_leaf_planted_refused (save_to_path_inner with the hook planting an outward leaf symlink returns Err whose Debug-formatted message contains MT_FS_PATH_DENIED, and the outside target's bytes are unchanged) and snapshot_race_leaf_planted_refused (write_document_snapshot_inner with a full DocumentWriteRequest fixture and the same planted mutation returns Err("MT_DOCUMENT_WRITE_FAILED"), the outside target's bytes are unchanged, and the early ownership-fence behavior at line 337 is untouched). No m001 error string or SavedTabState/DocumentWriteReply shape changes.

Red-first proof, recorded in the task evidence: with the five new tests authored, temporarily restore write_validated_bytes to the pre-fix body (single fence, create_dir_all, File::create on the once-validated path) and observe all five race tests fail exactly because the planted mutations succeed and bytes land on the outside target; restore the T-001 body and observe the same five pass — the spec's fails-before/passes-after criterion exercised inside one worktree without any commit. Allowance regressions stay green with NO modification to their code or expectations: fs.rs ancestor_inward_ok, ancestor_existing_outside_regression, ancestor_dangling_leaf_refused, write_creates_parent_dirs_when_missing, write_overwrites_existing_file, read_write_utf8_roundtrip, write_outside_sandbox_rejected, write_binary_creates_parent_dirs; m010_security's full suite including the ancestor_escape_text_new / ancestor_escape_binary_new / ancestor_escape_mkdir matrix and symlink_inside_sandbox_allowed; the m001_save_close and m005_prefs suites. The anti-vacuity naming is pinned: every new test carries the exact name above so the verification filters cannot pass vacuously (cargo exits 0 on a filter matching zero tests).
